recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. The current source already implements FHIR-19751 as refined by FHIR-34417, so further source changes would be redundant.
issue_request: FHIR-19751 was Published with a Persuasive resolution for R5 and requested a Range-like constraint enforcing that Period.start is less than or equal to Period.end when both are present.
initial_application: The Period datatype already had a per-1 invariant in source history. Commit c4807a5165ee632872ef9f6289fee8e9e1abbb5f explicitly listed FHIR-19751 and changed the invariant's human wording from a strict lower-than statement to lower-or-equal, while retaining the <= intent in the expressions.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini lists Period as an active datatype and maps datatype pages to datatypes.html. Later Published issue FHIR-34417 intentionally refined the same per-1 expression to use lowBoundary()/highBoundary() so different date/time precisions can be represented without weakening the start <= end rule. Searches found no Zulip or Confluence evidence that conflicts with the Jira/source conclusion.
reconciliation: No source edit was needed. source/datatypes/period.xml currently states that start SHALL have a lower or equal value than end and uses start.hasValue().not() or end.hasValue().not() or (start.lowBoundary() <= end.highBoundary()).

related_jiras.note: Later Published/R5 issue updated the same per-1 invariant expression to handle differing date/time precision while preserving the start <= end rule.
